**About the Project**

Based on the wide range of degree programs represented across the school, the faculty recruitment guidebook is organized by specific doctoral degree fields. Each section corresponds to detailed CIP (Classification of Instructional Programs) codes—for example, Africana Studies, Anthropology, or Chemistry—and includes data visualizations showing national trends in doctorate attainment by race, gender, and institution. This structure supports faculty search committees in making equity-informed decisions tailored to their academic area.


</div>





<div class="text-box">

**About the Data Source**

All data used in this project were collected from the *IPEDS Custom Data Center (IPEDS Builder_C)* a publicly accessible tool provided by the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES). The IPEDS Builder_C allows users to customize data  from the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), which is a comprehensive national database of U.S. postsecondary institutions.


<figure style="text-align:center; margin-top:40px;">
  <img src="images/IPEDS.png"
       alt="Screenshot of the Online IPEDS Data Builder"

  <figcaption style="margin-top:12px; font-style:italic;">

  </figcaption>

For this project, we extracted data on earned doctorates from academic years 2021 to 2023, disaggregated by Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) code, gender, race and ethnicity, institution name, and award level. This level of granularity enables us to present detailed visualizations that highlight demographic patterns across specific fields of doctoral study, (specifically, research based doctoral attainees). All data reflect self-reported institutional submissions to the U.S. Department of Education.
